title: Robert Bell / Article XIV — watch the proposition change
question: What did the applicant-side record actually claim about Robert Bell and Article XIV, and when did the government turn that body into a specific identity comparison?
non_goal: This does not assume the family originally claimed that their Robert Bell was the particular Article XIV Robert found in a government comparator record. It does not decide historical identity, Article XIV compliance, entitlement, or whether the 1902 administrative conclusion was correct.

proposition.short: Applicant pleading → Commission framing → identity comparator
proposition.identity_state: NO SINGLE IDENTITY PROPOSITION AT ENTRY / COMPARATOR APPEARS LATER

carriers.verb: KNOW / DO NOT KNOW / HAVE NOT HEARD
carriers.claim: The inspected oral examinations do not supply a uniform family proposition that their Robert Bell was a particular Article XIV Robert in a government record. Witnesses repeatedly preserve nonknowledge, told knowledge, or nonaffirmation about Article XIV.
carriers.change: Start with family knowledge as actually spoken. No specific two-Robert identity comparator is safely present here.
carriers.source: MCR 879 individual examination packets; proposition genealogy jacket 15HtKO-5KWQpwFDpi2FAgkbZYVRGI3gBOUCZkfqoitOc

carriers.object: applications, petitions, affidavits and attached documentary bodies
carriers.claim: The sixteen controlled applicant-side written pleadings carry Article XIV allegations in source-local forms. William D. Bell's petition, for example, says on information and belief that Robert Bell was duly enrolled in Mississippi under Article XIV. That pleading is not William's firsthand oral knowledge, and the origin of the recurring legal formulation remains open.
carriers.change: An affirmative Article XIV legal allegation enters the filed case. This still does not by itself establish that the applicants framed their claim as identity with the particular Article XIV Robert later selected from government records.
carriers.source: All sixteen applicant-side written pleading occurrences are now returned under source-facing control; packet-specific attached evidence remains distinct.

carriers.actor: Commission to the Five Civilized Tribes
carriers.claim: The Commission consolidates the applications as claims from a common ancestor and says at group scale that 'they claim' Robert Bell took advantage of Article XIV.
carriers.change: A compound applicant-side body becomes one Commission-authored group characterization. The Commission's 'they claim' formulation must not be back-assigned verbatim to family testimony or treated as proof that the family originated the later comparator frame.

carriers.actor: Commission to the Five Civilized Tribes
carriers.claim: The Commission brings a positive Article XIV Robert Bell record into the decision and then says the Robert shown by that record is not the same Robert through whom the applicants claim.
carriers.change: This is where the controlled body visibly becomes a specific identity comparison: claimant-line Robert versus record-side Article XIV Robert. The comparator is an administrative construction, not a proposition silently donated backward to the family.

carriers.claim: The Office uses its own record holdings, including a Robert Bell patent record and an Office-held Mississippi map, and carries forward a two-Robert administrative analysis.
carriers.change: The comparator body gains additional federal carriers and the two-Robert conclusion is independently restated at a new office layer.
carriers.source: Office of Indian Affairs report, 13 May 1902; governing source jacket 1U1KJ-si1F04WO7U8AasDLaNHFSykIzvAwfK6GJgky1w

carriers.claim: Interior says the records show one Robert Bell did comply with Article XIV, while the applicants' alleged ancestor is not the identical person; it approves the Commission's action and affirms the decision.
carriers.change: The identity-conditioned exclusion becomes the Department's operative administrative disposition.

refusals.proposal: The family's original claim was that their Robert Bell was the specific Article XIV Robert in the government's comparator record.
refusals.reason: The controlled applicant-side pleadings do carry Article XIV allegations, but the present source genealogy does not establish that the family originated the later government-record identity comparator. Oral family testimony often preserves nonknowledge; the Commission later consolidates the body as 'they claim' and then constructs the specific record-side comparison.

refusals.proposal: The applicants testified that Robert Bell took advantage of Article XIV.
refusals.reason: The inspected oral testimony contains repeated nonknowledge and nonaffirmation. The affirmative proposition appears in written pleadings and later Commission characterization. Speaker and source layer changed.

refusals.proposal: The government denied the claim because there was no Article XIV Robert Bell record.
refusals.reason: The 1902 administrative sequence recognizes a positive Article XIV Robert Bell record. The adverse result follows an identity partition: the recorded compliant Robert is assigned to a different person from the applicants' alleged ancestor.

refusals.proposal: The Commission's NOT IDENTICAL finding proves the two Roberts were historically different people.
refusals.reason: NOT IDENTICAL is an attributed administrative finding in MCR 879. The Workshop does not promote that case-local identity operator into independent historical fact.

open: Whether the recurring applicant-side Article XIV pleading language originated with applicants, counsel, a form/template, or another filing practice remains open.
Historical identity of the Robert Bell occurrences remains unresolved at the Workshop level.
The exact completeness and formation history of the Commission and Indian Office comparator populations remain open.
The exact object genealogy of every affirmative applicant-side Article XIV proposition remains packet-specific.
The post-Interior downward return carrier remains an open documentary interval.
